description: Set up an appointment booking system: define services, configure availability, build the booking interface, set notifications and policies.

steps.description: Define the service menu for the booking system, including service types, durations, and assigned providers.

inputs.name: business-type
inputs.desc: The type of business or practice offering appointments

inputs.name: services-list
inputs.desc: Draft list of services to offer for booking

outputs.name: service-catalog
outputs.desc: Finalized catalog of bookable services with name, duration, price, and assigned provider(s)

outputs.name: service-constraints
outputs.desc: Constraints per service (required equipment, room type, prep time, follow-up time)

process: List every distinct service the business offers, including variations (e.g., initial vs. follow-up visit).
For each service, record the name, default duration, price (if applicable), and which providers can perform it.
Note any constraints: required room type, equipment, prep or cleanup time between appointments.
Produce the service catalog as a structured list ready for the booking platform.

steps.description: Configure the availability rules that control when appointments can be booked.

outputs.name: availability-rules
outputs.desc: Complete set of availability rules (hours, breaks, buffer, lead time, blackout dates)

outputs.name: provider-schedules
outputs.desc: Per-provider weekly schedule templates

process: Define the business hours for each day of the week, including any seasonal variations.
Set buffer time between appointments (travel time, cleanup, transition).
Configure minimum and maximum lead time for bookings (e.g., at least 2 hours ahead, no more than 90 days out).
Define blackout dates (holidays, closures) and recurring breaks (lunch, admin blocks).
For multi-provider setups, build a per-provider weekly schedule template.

steps.description: Set up the customer-facing booking page or widget where appointments are scheduled.

inputs.name: availability-rules
inputs.desc: Availability rules governing when slots appear

outputs.name: booking-page-config
outputs.desc: Configuration of the booking page (layout, fields, branding, embed code)

outputs.name: intake-form-fields
outputs.desc: Customer intake fields collected at booking time

process: Select the booking platform or embed method (standalone page, website widget, link in email).
Configure the booking flow: service selection, provider selection (if applicable), date/time picker, customer info form.
Define the intake fields to collect at booking (name, contact, reason for visit, insurance, special requests).
Apply branding (logo, colors, confirmation copy) and test the booking flow end to end.

steps.description: Configure the automated notifications sent before, during, and after the booking lifecycle.

outputs.name: notification-templates
outputs.desc: Templates for confirmation, reminder, follow-up, and cancellation notifications

outputs.name: notification-schedule
outputs.desc: Timing rules for each notification (e.g., reminder 24h before, follow-up 1 day after)

process: Write the confirmation notification sent immediately after booking (include date, time, location, prep instructions).
Write the reminder notification(s) sent before the appointment (e.g., 24 hours and 1 hour before).
Write the follow-up notification sent after the appointment (thank you, feedback request, rebooking link).
Write the cancellation and reschedule notifications.
Define the delivery channel for each (email, SMS, or both) and the send timing.

steps.description: Define the cancellation, rescheduling, and no-show policies for the booking system.

inputs.name: notification-templates
inputs.desc: Notification templates that will reference the policy

inputs.name: service-catalog
inputs.desc: Services catalog for policy variation by service type

outputs.name: cancellation-policy
outputs.desc: The published cancellation, rescheduling, and no-show policy

outputs.name: booking-system-document
outputs.desc: Complete booking system setup document combining all configuration

process: Define the cancellation window (e.g., free cancellation up to 24 hours before, fee after that).
Define the rescheduling rules (how many times, how far in advance, same-day allowed or not).
Define the no-show policy (fee, automatic rebooking, follow-up action).
Publish the policy on the booking page and include it in the confirmation notification.
Compile the complete booking system setup document: service catalog, availability rules, booking page, notifications, and policies.

description: Manage staff or resource availability: collect preferences, define scheduling rules, build the master calendar, handle time-off requests.

steps.description: Collect individual availability preferences from staff or resource owners.

inputs.name: team-roster
inputs.desc: List of staff or resources whose availability needs to be managed

inputs.name: scheduling-period
inputs.desc: The time period being scheduled (week, month, quarter)

outputs.name: individual-preferences
outputs.desc: Each person's preferred hours, days off, constraints, and hard limits

outputs.name: preference-conflicts
outputs.desc: Conflicts between individual preferences and business needs

process: Send each team member an availability form covering the scheduling period.
Collect preferred working hours, preferred days off, hard constraints (school pickup, second job, medical), and overtime willingness.
Identify conflicts between individual preferences and the coverage requirements.
Flag any unresolvable conflicts for manager review.

steps.description: Define the rules that govern how availability translates into scheduled time.

inputs.name: preference-conflicts
inputs.desc: Identified conflicts between preferences and needs

outputs.name: scheduling-rules
outputs.desc: Complete ruleset (min/max hours, consecutive limits, overtime triggers, fairness rotation)

outputs.name: coverage-requirements
outputs.desc: Minimum staffing levels by time slot and role

process: Set the minimum and maximum hours per person per week.
Define consecutive day limits (e.g., no more than 6 days in a row without a day off).
Set overtime thresholds and approval rules.
Define fairness rules (rotate weekends, distribute holidays, balance desirable and undesirable shifts).
Document the minimum coverage requirements by time slot and role.

steps.description: Build the master availability calendar that combines all individual schedules and rules.

inputs.name: coverage-requirements
inputs.desc: Minimum staffing levels by time slot

outputs.name: master-calendar
outputs.desc: The consolidated availability calendar showing who is available when

outputs.name: coverage-gaps
outputs.desc: Time slots where coverage falls below the minimum requirement

process: Overlay all individual availability onto a single calendar view.
Apply the scheduling rules to filter out violations (overtime, consecutive day limits).
Identify coverage gaps where available staff falls below the minimum requirement.
Propose solutions for gaps (shift trades, on-call assignments, temporary staff).
Publish the master calendar to the scheduling system.

steps.description: Handle time-off requests and approvals against the master calendar.

outputs.name: time-off-decisions
outputs.desc: Approved and denied time-off requests with rationale

outputs.name: updated-calendar
outputs.desc: Master calendar updated with approved time off

process: Receive the time-off request (dates, reason, partial or full day).
Check coverage impact: will the absence create a gap below minimum staffing?
If coverage is adequate, approve and update the calendar. If not, check for volunteers or swaps.
Notify the requester of the decision and update the master calendar.

steps.description: Publish the finalized availability to all downstream booking and scheduling systems.

inputs.name: updated-calendar
inputs.desc: The master calendar with all updates applied

outputs.name: published-availability
outputs.desc: The availability as published to booking systems and team members

outputs.name: availability-management-plan
outputs.desc: Complete availability management plan documenting the process and rules

process: Push the updated availability to the appointment booking system so customers see accurate open slots.
Notify team members of their finalized schedules.
Set up alerts for last-minute changes (callouts, emergencies) that require immediate re-publication.
Compile the availability management plan documenting the full process, rules, and escalation paths.

description: Synchronize calendars across multiple systems: inventory sources, define sync rules, configure connections, and monitor for failures.

steps.description: Inventory all calendar sources that need to be synchronized.

inputs.name: user-or-team
inputs.desc: The person or team whose calendars need syncing

inputs.name: current-tools
inputs.desc: The calendar and scheduling tools currently in use

outputs.name: calendar-inventory
outputs.desc: List of all calendar sources with platform, purpose, and owner

outputs.name: sync-needs
outputs.desc: Which calendars need to share data and in what direction

process: List every calendar the user or team touches (personal Google/Outlook, work calendar, booking system, project management, shared team calendars).
For each calendar, note the platform, owner, primary purpose, and whether it is the source of truth for any event type.
Identify which pairs of calendars need to sync and whether the sync is one-way or bidirectional.
Note any calendars that must remain private (show busy/free only, not event details).

steps.description: Define the synchronization rules including direction, conflict resolution, and field mapping.

outputs.name: sync-rules
outputs.desc: Complete sync ruleset (direction, conflict resolution, field mapping, filters)

outputs.name: timezone-handling
outputs.desc: Rules for handling timezone differences across calendars

process: For each sync pair, define the direction (one-way push, one-way pull, bidirectional).
Define conflict resolution: if the same time slot has events on both sides, which calendar wins?
Define field mapping: which fields copy (title, location, attendees, description) and which are blocked (private notes, internal links).
Define timezone handling: store in UTC, display in local, convert on sync.
Set filters: which event types sync (meetings yes, all-day reminders no, tentative events as busy blocks).

steps.description: Configure the actual sync connections between calendar systems.

outputs.name: sync-connections
outputs.desc: Configured and tested sync connections between each calendar pair

outputs.name: sync-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of the initial sync test (events synced correctly, conflicts handled)

process: Select the sync tool or integration method for each pair (native integration, third-party sync service, API-based custom sync).
Authenticate and connect each calendar source.
Apply the sync rules (direction, field mapping, filters, timezone handling).
Run an initial sync and verify that events appear correctly on both sides.
Test conflict scenarios to confirm the resolution rules work as defined.

steps.description: Set up monitoring for sync failures and drift between calendars.

outputs.name: sync-monitoring-config
outputs.desc: Monitoring configuration (alerts, health checks, logs)

outputs.name: calendar-sync-document
outputs.desc: Complete calendar sync setup document

process: Set up alerts for sync failures (connection lost, authentication expired, quota exceeded).
Configure a periodic health check that compares event counts and recent changes across synced calendars.
Set up logging so sync errors can be diagnosed (which event, which direction, what went wrong).
Compile the complete calendar sync document: inventory, rules, connections, monitoring, and troubleshooting steps.

description: Audit and optimize recurring meetings: score each for necessity, recommend changes, and measure time recovered.

steps.description: Audit all recurring meetings on the calendar to build a complete inventory.

inputs.name: calendar-access
inputs.desc: Access to the calendar(s) containing recurring meetings

inputs.name: audit-scope
inputs.desc: Whose meetings to audit (individual, team, department)

outputs.name: meeting-inventory
outputs.desc: List of all recurring meetings with frequency, duration, attendee count, and stated purpose

outputs.name: time-commitment
outputs.desc: Total hours per week spent in recurring meetings by person

process: Pull all recurring events from the calendar(s) in scope.
For each meeting, record: title, frequency, duration, number of attendees, organizer, and stated purpose.
Calculate the total hours per week each person spends in recurring meetings.
Flag meetings with no stated agenda or purpose, meetings with more than 8 attendees, and meetings that have been recurring for more than 6 months without review.

steps.description: Score each recurring meeting on necessity and effectiveness.

inputs.name: time-commitment
inputs.desc: Hours per week in recurring meetings

outputs.name: meeting-scores
outputs.desc: Each meeting scored on necessity (1-5) and effectiveness (1-5) with rationale

outputs.name: low-value-meetings
outputs.desc: Meetings scoring below threshold on necessity or effectiveness

process: For each meeting, score necessity (1-5): does a decision or handoff depend on this meeting happening synchronously?
Score effectiveness (1-5): does the meeting consistently produce its intended output (decisions, updates, alignment)?
Survey attendees (optional) for their perception of value and whether they need to attend.
Flag meetings scoring below 3 on either dimension as candidates for change.

steps.description: Recommend specific changes for each low-value recurring meeting.

outputs.name: change-recommendations
outputs.desc: Specific recommendation for each meeting (cancel, reduce frequency, shorten, combine, make async)

outputs.name: projected-time-savings
outputs.desc: Projected hours recovered per week if recommendations are adopted

process: For each low-value meeting, recommend one action: cancel entirely, reduce frequency (weekly to biweekly), shorten duration, combine with another meeting, or convert to async (written update, shared doc).
For meetings to keep, recommend attendee list trimming if some people are optional.
Calculate the projected time savings per week for each recommendation.
Present the recommendations to the meeting organizers for approval.

steps.description: Implement the approved meeting changes and update the calendar.

outputs.name: implemented-changes
outputs.desc: Record of which changes were made to which meetings

outputs.name: optimization-report
outputs.desc: Complete meeting optimization report with before/after metrics

process: For each approved change, update the calendar event (cancel, change recurrence, shorten, update attendees).
Notify all affected attendees of the change and the reason.
For meetings converted to async, set up the replacement (shared doc, Slack channel, weekly written update).
After 4 weeks, measure actual time recovered and compare to projections.
Compile the optimization report with before and after metrics.

description: Set up a shared resource booking system for rooms, equipment, vehicles, or desks with conflict detection and access rules.

steps.description: Inventory the shared resources that will be available for booking.

inputs.name: resource-types
inputs.desc: Types of resources to manage (rooms, equipment, vehicles, desks, other)

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: The organization or facility where resources are located

outputs.name: resource-catalog
outputs.desc: Catalog of bookable resources with name, type, location, capacity, and features

outputs.name: resource-rules
outputs.desc: Per-resource booking rules (advance notice, max duration, cleanup time, approval required)

process: List every shared resource that should be bookable, grouped by type.
For each resource, record: name, type, location, capacity (for rooms), features (AV equipment, whiteboard, wheelchair accessible), and photo if helpful.
Define the booking rules per resource: minimum advance notice, maximum booking duration, buffer/cleanup time between bookings, and whether approval is required.
Note any resources with restricted access (executive conference room, specialized equipment requiring certification).

steps.description: Configure the booking rules and access permissions for shared resources.

outputs.name: access-permissions
outputs.desc: Who can book which resources, with any approval chains

outputs.name: booking-policies
outputs.desc: Policies for cancellation, no-show, recurring bookings, and priority/override

process: Define who can book each resource (all staff, specific departments, requires manager approval).
Set the cancellation policy (free up to X hours before, auto-release if not checked in within 15 minutes).
Define recurring booking rules (allowed or not, max weeks ahead, auto-renewal).
Set priority rules for conflicts (first come first served, department priority, seniority).

steps.description: Build the interface where users search for and book available resources.

inputs.name: access-permissions
inputs.desc: Access rules for who can book what

outputs.name: booking-interface
outputs.desc: The configured booking interface (calendar view, search filters, booking form)

outputs.name: conflict-detection-config
outputs.desc: Conflict detection and waitlist configuration

process: Build the resource search: filter by type, date/time, capacity, features, and location.
Show availability in a calendar view with real-time conflict detection.
Configure the booking form: resource selected, date/time, duration, purpose, attendees.
Set up waitlisting for popular resources (add to waitlist, notify when slot opens).
Test the full booking flow including conflict detection and waitlist.

steps.description: Track resource utilization to inform future capacity decisions.

outputs.name: utilization-dashboard
outputs.desc: Dashboard showing booking rates, no-show rates, peak times, and underused resources

outputs.name: resource-booking-document
outputs.desc: Complete resource booking system setup document

process: Track booking rate per resource (percentage of available hours booked).
Track no-show and cancellation rates per resource.
Identify peak demand times and resources with frequent waitlists (candidates for adding capacity).
Identify underused resources (candidates for repurposing or removing from the system).
Compile the complete resource booking system document: catalog, rules, interface, and utilization baseline.

description: Schedule field or on-site services: match requests to providers, confirm appointments, handle day-of changes.

steps.description: Receive and triage the service request to determine scheduling requirements.

inputs.name: service-request
inputs.desc: The customer's service request (type, urgency, location, preferences)

inputs.name: service-area-map
inputs.desc: The geographic service area and zone definitions

outputs.name: triaged-request
outputs.desc: Request classified by service type, urgency, zone, estimated duration, and required skills

outputs.name: scheduling-constraints
outputs.desc: Constraints on when the service can be scheduled (customer availability, parts needed, permits)

process: Receive the service request and extract: service type, location, urgency level, and customer preferences.
Classify the request by zone (geographic area) and estimate the duration based on service type.
Identify any prerequisites (parts need to be ordered, permits required, previous visit notes to review).
Determine the customer's available time windows for the appointment.

steps.description: Match the service request to an available provider based on skills, location, and schedule.

outputs.name: matched-providers
outputs.desc: Ranked list of available providers who can fulfill the request

outputs.name: proposed-slots
outputs.desc: Proposed appointment time slots based on provider availability and customer preferences

process: Query the provider roster for those with the required skills and certifications.
Filter by zone (prefer providers already working nearby to minimize travel time).
Check each provider's calendar for open slots that align with the customer's availability.
Rank the matches by fit (skills, proximity, schedule efficiency) and present the top options.

steps.description: Confirm the appointment with the customer and calendar it for the provider.

outputs.name: confirmed-appointment
outputs.desc: The confirmed appointment with date, time, provider, and customer details

outputs.name: pre-visit-checklist
outputs.desc: Pre-visit instructions for both the customer and the provider

process: Present the proposed time slots to the customer and confirm their selection.
Book the appointment on the provider's calendar and block travel time before and after.
Send the confirmation to the customer with date, time, provider name, and what to expect.
Send the provider their pre-visit checklist (service details, customer notes, location, required tools/parts).

steps.description: Handle same-day changes to the service schedule (cancellations, delays, emergencies).

outputs.name: schedule-adjustment
outputs.desc: The adjustment made (reschedule, reassign, cancel) and its downstream impact

outputs.name: service-scheduling-record
outputs.desc: Complete service scheduling record for this request

process: Receive the change trigger (customer cancels, provider is delayed, emergency takes priority).
Assess the impact: can the slot be backfilled? Does the delay cascade into later appointments?
Execute the adjustment: reschedule with the same provider, reassign to another provider, or cancel and rebook.
Notify all affected parties (customer, provider, dispatcher) and update the calendar.
Record the complete service scheduling lifecycle for this request.

description: Build employee shift schedules: define coverage needs, collect preferences, generate and publish the schedule.

steps.description: Define the shift types and coverage requirements by time period.

inputs.name: business-hours
inputs.desc: The operating hours of the business

inputs.name: staffing-model
inputs.desc: The staffing model (roles, skill levels, minimum coverage by role)

outputs.name: shift-types
outputs.desc: Defined shift types with start/end times, break schedules, and applicable roles

outputs.name: coverage-matrix
outputs.desc: Required headcount by shift type, day of week, and role

process: Divide the operating hours into shift blocks (morning, afternoon, evening, overnight as applicable).
For each shift, define the start and end times, break duration and timing, and which roles are needed.
Build the coverage matrix: how many of each role are needed for each shift on each day of the week.
Account for seasonal or event-based variations in coverage needs.

steps.description: Collect employee shift preferences, constraints, and availability for the scheduling period.

inputs.name: coverage-matrix
inputs.desc: Coverage requirements by shift and day

outputs.name: employee-preferences
outputs.desc: Each employee's preferred shifts, hard constraints, and availability for the period

outputs.name: preference-summary
outputs.desc: Summary showing which shifts are overstaffed and understaffed based on preferences

process: Send the preference form to all eligible employees for the upcoming scheduling period.
Collect: preferred shifts (ranked), days they cannot work (with reason), overtime willingness, and swap willingness.
Summarize preferences against the coverage matrix to identify which shifts will be easy to fill and which will be short.
Flag employees who have not submitted preferences by the deadline.

steps.description: Generate the shift schedule by assigning employees to shifts based on coverage needs, preferences, and rules.

inputs.name: preference-summary
inputs.desc: Summary of overstaffed and understaffed shifts

outputs.name: draft-schedule
outputs.desc: The draft schedule with employees assigned to shifts for the period

outputs.name: schedule-violations
outputs.desc: Any rule violations in the draft (overtime, consecutive days, fairness imbalances)

process: Start with the hardest-to-fill shifts (weekends, overnights, holidays) and assign based on availability and rotation fairness.
Fill remaining shifts by matching preferences to open slots.
Check for rule violations: overtime thresholds, consecutive day limits, required rest between shifts, fairness rotation.
Resolve violations by swapping assignments or flagging for manager decision.
Produce the draft schedule for review.

steps.description: Handle shift swap requests, callouts, and schedule changes after publication.

outputs.name: swap-log
outputs.desc: Record of all swap requests with outcomes (approved, denied, pending)

outputs.name: schedule-change-record
outputs.desc: All post-publication changes to the schedule

process: Receive the swap request (employee A wants to trade shift X with employee B's shift Y).
Validate: both employees are qualified for the other's shift, no rule violations result from the swap.
If valid, approve and update the schedule. Notify both employees.
For callouts (sick, emergency), find a replacement from the on-call list or offer the shift to all qualified staff.

steps.description: Finalize and publish the shift schedule to all employees.

outputs.name: published-schedule
outputs.desc: The finalized, published schedule accessible to all employees

outputs.name: shift-scheduling-record
outputs.desc: Complete shift scheduling record for the period

process: Review the final schedule for completeness (all shifts covered, no rule violations).
Publish to the scheduling system and notify all employees of their assigned shifts.
Set the deadline for the next round of swap requests.
Compile the shift scheduling record: coverage achieved, preference fulfillment rate, overtime hours, and fairness metrics.

description: Schedule a multi-session event or conference: collect proposals, assign sessions to rooms and time slots, handle last-minute changes.

steps.description: Collect session proposals and speaker availability for the event.

inputs.name: event-details
inputs.desc: Event name, dates, venue, expected attendance, and theme

inputs.name: call-for-proposals
inputs.desc: The criteria and format for session proposals

outputs.name: session-proposals
outputs.desc: All submitted proposals with title, speaker, duration, topic, AV needs, and speaker availability

outputs.name: speaker-availability
outputs.desc: Each speaker's available and unavailable time slots during the event

process: Publish the call for proposals with the submission format, topics, and deadline.
Collect proposals: title, abstract, speaker name and bio, session format (talk, panel, workshop), requested duration, AV/room requirements.
Collect each speaker's availability across the event dates (travel constraints, other commitments, preferred time of day).
Review and accept proposals based on the evaluation criteria. Notify accepted and declined speakers.

steps.description: Define the room and time slot grid for the event schedule.

outputs.name: slot-grid
outputs.desc: The time slot grid (rows = time blocks, columns = rooms) with capacity and features per room

outputs.name: scheduling-constraints
outputs.desc: Hard constraints (speaker conflicts, room requirements, attendee flow limits)

process: Define the time blocks for each day (morning sessions, lunch, afternoon sessions, evening).
Map the available rooms with capacity, AV equipment, and features.
Build the grid: each cell is a room-plus-time-slot that can hold one session.
List the hard constraints: no speaker in two sessions at the same time, workshops need specific rooms, keynotes in the main hall.

steps.description: Assign sessions to rooms and time slots, respecting all constraints.

inputs.name: slot-grid
inputs.desc: The room and time slot grid

outputs.name: draft-event-schedule
outputs.desc: Draft schedule with each session assigned to a room and time slot

outputs.name: assignment-conflicts
outputs.desc: Any unresolved conflicts or suboptimal placements

process: Place keynotes and fixed-time sessions first (opening, closing, sponsored slots).
Assign remaining sessions by priority: speaker availability narrows options, room requirements filter further, topic clustering fills the rest.
Check for speaker conflicts (same speaker in overlapping slots) and attendee flow issues (popular sessions back-to-back in distant rooms).
Identify and resolve conflicts by swapping slots or adjusting room assignments.
Produce the draft schedule for review.

steps.description: Finalize and publish the event schedule, then handle last-minute changes.

outputs.name: published-event-schedule
outputs.desc: The published event schedule (web, app, printed program)

outputs.name: event-schedule-record
outputs.desc: Complete event scheduling record including change log

process: Review the draft with speakers and stakeholders for final corrections.
Publish the schedule to the event website, mobile app, and printed program.
Set up a change protocol for last-minute issues (speaker cancellation, room change, time swap).
When a change occurs, update all published channels and notify affected attendees.
After the event, compile the scheduling record with lessons learned for next time.

description: Manage recurring client sessions (coaching, therapy, tutoring): set cadence, track history, handle reschedules, manage packages.

steps.description: Set up the recurring session cadence for a client.

inputs.name: client-profile
inputs.desc: The client's name, contact info, service type, and goals

inputs.name: provider-availability
inputs.desc: The provider's available time slots for recurring sessions

outputs.name: session-cadence
outputs.desc: The agreed cadence (weekly, biweekly, monthly), day, time, and duration

outputs.name: session-package
outputs.desc: The session package or subscription details (number of sessions, expiration, price)

process: Discuss the client's preferred frequency (weekly, biweekly, monthly) and time preferences.
Match against the provider's available recurring slots.
Confirm the cadence: day, time, duration, and modality (in-person, video, phone).
Set up the package or subscription: number of prepaid sessions, expiration date, cancellation terms.

steps.description: Track session history, notes, and progress for the client.

outputs.name: session-log
outputs.desc: Running log of completed sessions with date, duration, key topics, and action items

outputs.name: package-usage
outputs.desc: Sessions used, sessions remaining, next renewal or expiration date

process: After each session, record the date, actual duration, key topics discussed, and action items assigned.
Track progress toward the client's stated goals.
Update the package usage count (sessions used, remaining, expiration warning if nearing the end).
Flag when a client is due for a progress review or package renewal.

steps.description: Handle reschedules, cancellations, and no-shows for client sessions.

outputs.name: reschedule-record
outputs.desc: Record of reschedules, cancellations, and no-shows with reasons and outcomes

outputs.name: attendance-pattern
outputs.desc: Pattern analysis (frequent cancellations, no-show streaks, preferred reschedule times)

process: When a reschedule request comes in, check the cancellation policy (within window = free, late = fee or lost session).
Offer alternative times within the same week if possible, or the next available slot.
For no-shows, follow up with the client (check in, remind of the policy, offer to rebook).
Track patterns: if a client frequently cancels a specific day or time, suggest changing the recurring cadence.

steps.description: Send session preparation materials and reminders to the client before each session.

outputs.name: prep-materials
outputs.desc: Pre-session materials sent to the client (homework review, agenda, reading)

outputs.name: session-management-record
outputs.desc: Complete session management record for this client

process: 24-48 hours before the session, send a reminder with date, time, and modality.
Include any prep materials: homework to complete, questions to think about, documents to review.
Include a brief summary of the last session's action items so the client can report on progress.
Compile the complete session management record: cadence, history, attendance, package status, and notes.

description: Manage a booking waitlist: add customers, notify when slots open, fill from the waitlist, track conversion rates.

steps.description: Add a customer to the waitlist when the desired slot or service is full.

inputs.name: waitlist-request
inputs.desc: The customer's request (desired service, date/time range, contact info)

inputs.name: current-availability
inputs.desc: Current booking availability showing the full slots

outputs.name: waitlist-entry
outputs.desc: The waitlist record (customer, desired slot, priority, position, expiration)

outputs.name: waitlist-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation sent to the customer with their position and expected wait

process: Confirm the slot is genuinely full (not just showing unavailable due to a hold or buffer).
Create the waitlist entry: customer contact, desired service, acceptable date/time range, and any flexibility notes.
Assign a position based on the priority rules (first come, VIP, urgency).
Send the customer a confirmation with their position and estimated wait time.

steps.description: Notify the next person on the waitlist when a slot opens up.

inputs.name: waitlist-entry
inputs.desc: The waitlist entries for the opened slot

inputs.name: current-availability
inputs.desc: Updated availability showing the opened slot

outputs.name: notification-sent
outputs.desc: Notification sent to the next eligible person with response deadline

outputs.name: response-window
outputs.desc: The expiration window for the offer (e.g., 4 hours to respond)

process: Detect the slot opening (cancellation, schedule extension, new provider added).
Identify the next person on the waitlist whose desired range matches the opened slot.
Send a notification via their preferred channel (SMS, email, app notification) with the slot details.
Set a response deadline (e.g., respond within 4 hours or the offer moves to the next person).

steps.description: Fill the opened slot from the waitlist based on responses.

inputs.name: notification-sent
inputs.desc: Notification sent to the waitlist candidate

outputs.name: slot-filled
outputs.desc: Whether the slot was filled and by whom, or moved to the next candidate

outputs.name: waitlist-updated
outputs.desc: Updated waitlist with the filled entry removed and positions adjusted

process: If the candidate accepts within the window, book the slot and remove them from the waitlist.
If the candidate declines or does not respond, move to the next eligible person and repeat the offer.
If the waitlist is exhausted, release the slot to general availability.
Update all waitlist positions and notify remaining waitlisted customers of their new position.

steps.description: Track waitlist performance metrics and conversion rates.

outputs.name: waitlist-metrics
outputs.desc: Conversion rate, average wait time, abandonment rate, fill rate by service type

outputs.name: waitlist-management-record
outputs.desc: Complete waitlist management report

process: Calculate the conversion rate (waitlisted customers who ultimately booked divided by total waitlisted).
Calculate the average wait time from joining the waitlist to booking or abandoning.
Track abandonment rate (customers who removed themselves or expired without booking).
Identify services or time slots with chronic waitlists (candidates for adding capacity).
Compile the waitlist management report with metrics and recommendations.
